record.original_question: Suppose f : (-infinity, 0] x R^3 -> [0, infinity) is a smooth classical solution of the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation, satisfies 0 <= f(t, v) <= 1 everywhere, and for every time t there is a constant C_t with integral f(v) <v>^{-1} dv <= C_t. Must f be a stationary Maxwellian?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.5. Let f : (−∞, 0] × R3 → [0, ∞) be a smooth classical solution of (7.1), where Q is the Landau-Coulomb operator (7.2). We make the following assumptions. • For all (t, v) ∈ (−∞, 0] × R3 , we have 0 ≤ f (t, v) ≤ 1. • For every t ∈ (−∞, 0], there is some constant Ct so that f (v)hvi−1 dv ≤ Ct . Then f must be a stationary Maxwellian.
However, a positive resolution of Conjecture 7.5 seems to be very difficult with current techniques.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(-\infty,0]\times\mathbb{R}^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a smooth classical solution of the spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential
$$\partial_t f(t,v) \;=\; Q(f,f)(t,v), \qquad (t,v)\in(-\infty,0]\times\mathbb{R}^3,$$
where the Landau-Coulomb collision operator is
$$Q(f,f)(v) \;=\; \nabla_v\!\cdot\!\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} a(v-w)\bigl[f(w)\nabla f(v)-f(v)\nabla f(w)\bigr]\,dw\right),$$
with kernel
$$a(z) \;=\; \frac{1}{|z|}\left(I - \frac{z\otimes z}{|z|^2}\right).$$
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $0\le f(t,v)\le 1$ for all $(t,v)\in(-\infty,0]\times\mathbb{R}^3$;
\item for every $t\in(-\infty,0]$, there exists a constant $C_t$ such that
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} f(t,v)\,\langle v\rangle^{-1}\,dv \;\le\; C_t,$$
where $\langle v\rangle = (1+|v|^2)^{1/2}$.
\end{enumerate}
Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses $f$ must be a stationary Maxwellian, i.e.\ there exist constants $\rho\ge 0$, $T>0$, and $u\in\mathbb{R}^3$ (independent of $t$) such that
$$f(t,v) \;=\; \frac{\rho}{(2\pi T)^{3/2}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{|v-u|^2}{2T}\right).$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any proof of this Liouville-type rigidity statement for ancient bounded solutions of the spatially homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation. Related works address global existence in $L^{3/2}$, near-Maxwellian stability, and non-existence of Type-I self-similar blow-up, but not the full conjecture. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Global Smooth Solutions to the Landau-Coulomb Equation in L^{3/2}
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth solutions exist for positive times with polynomially weighted L^{3/2} initial data; Maxwellian behaviour forms only at larger times.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work concerns existence/regularity rather than rigidity of ancient bounded solutions.

status_evidence.title: Landau equation for very soft and Coulomb potentials near Maxwellians
status_evidence.snippet: Stability estimates near Maxwellian equilibrium for the linearized Landau operator.
status_evidence.claim: Existing near-Maxwellian results do not address the global Liouville-type rigidity question.
